subject.title: Feature/Fix: Add conservative lineage safety and promotion controls

question: Should CodexBar accept this lineage architecture as dormant legacy-default infrastructure now, and what exact evidence must be satisfied before lineage accounting may become authoritative?
rationale: Tests can verify the mechanics, but they cannot decide whether the remaining day-level accounting residuals and cache-transition risk are acceptable for an authority path that changes user-visible cost totals.

options.title: Require proof, keep legacy authoritative
options.body: Accept the architecture only after exact-head cache-transition and rollback proof, while leaving lineage promotion disabled until residual evidence receives a separate maintainer approval.

options.title: Accept dormant infrastructure now
options.body: Merge the ordered stack with legacy as the default and explicitly accept the remaining proof gap because no production caller currently receives promotion authorization.

options.title: Pause the authority layer
options.body: Defer this PR until the validation slice reduces day-level residuals and demonstrates the complete upgrade and retained-cache lifecycle.

recommendation.title: Require proof, keep legacy authoritative
recommendation.body: Accept the architecture only after exact-head cache-transition and rollback proof, while leaving lineage promotion disabled until residual evidence receives a separate maintainer approval.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged scanner refinements encode the current accounting invariants, and repository ownership makes this the clearest available product-authority decision route.
